702976.t: Traditionally derived from a dissimilation of an unattested earlier *γραστήρ (*grăstḗr, “devourer”), from γράω (grắō, “to gnaw, eat”) + -τήρ (-tḗr, agent noun suffix).

702953.t: From γάμος (gắmos, “marriage; matrimony”) + -έω (-éō, denominative verbal suffix) (though Beekes considers the noun a back-formation from the verb rather than the verb being derived from the noun).

702919.t: Possibly inherited from Proto-Indo-European *gláktn̥ (“milk”) (compare Latin lact, Old Armenian կաթն (katʻn), Albanian dhallë), earlier *glákt (or, if the Hittite cognate is valid, *gláktr̥), perhaps from a root *glag- + *-tr̥, but the phonetic…

702950.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ǵem- (“to marry”). Cognate with Sanskrit जामातृ (jā́mātṛ), Avestan 𐬰𐬁𐬨𐬁𐬙𐬀𐬭 (zāmātar).

702916.t: From Latin gaesum, itself from Gaulish *gaisos, from Proto-Celtic *gaisos (“spear”). Compare also χαῖος (khaîos, “shepherd's staff”), Sanskrit हेषस् (héṣas, “missile”).
